evidence: Abstract: '1 970 APIs will not always correctly inform their clients about breaking changes released as part of minor or patch-level upgrades' (of 3 075). Sec 4.2: '96 Breaking Changes, 66 Non-Breaking Changes, and 33 Undecidable Changes'; 'approx. one third of the changes are undecidable'. Sec 7.1 quote and single-tool oasdiff caveat confirmed.
correction: 1,970 of 3,075 APIs do not always signal breaking changes via major versions (Abstract); 33 of 195 change TYPES are undecidable, and approx. one third of observed CHANGES are undecidable (Sec 4.2, not Sec 3); Sec 7.1 notes subtle/indirect changes may go undetected and reliance on oasdiff alone may bias results. Authors: Souhaila Serbout, Cesare Pautasso (USI). Venue ICWE 2024 per URL filename [verify].

evidence: arXiv 2605.24397 (Chen, Bi, Wang, Thongtanunam, May 2026). Abstract: '43 detection approaches that reach high accuracy on syntactic breaks but limited coverage on behavioral ones.' Sec 3.1: 'These changes evade static detection and appear only during execution.'
correction: Quote is in Sec 3.1 'Nature of Breaking Changes (What)'; Sec 3.1.2 adds 'they bypass type systems and static analysis'. Sec 7 not checked [verify]. Preprint, not peer-reviewed.

evidence: Sec 3.3.2: 'Change Behavior BCs make up the largest proportion of all BC types (68.1%).' Sec 3.3.1: '1,519 commits that contain reason-related information.' Sec 4.1: 'a proportion (19%) of documented breaking changes cannot be detected via regression testing'.
correction: Authors Kong, Liu, Bao, Lo. The 1,519 are BC commits with reason information, not 1,519 BCs. arXiv page has no journal-ref; TOSEM 2025 venue [verify] (HTML template shows 'JACM').

evidence: Abstract (ISSTA '20, Godefroid, Lehmann, Polishchuk): 'across 17 different versions of the widely-used Azure networking APIs deployed between 2016 and 2019 detected 14 regressions in total, 5 of those in the official API specifications and 9 regressions in the services themselves.'
correction: Sec 2.3 defines service regressions as previously working requests that 'return different or wrong results' after a service update. Sec 4.6 is Threats to Validity; regression counts appear in Abstract and Sec 4.3/4.4, so cite Abstract + Sec 2.3.

evidence: Sec 4.2 (RQ2) Finding 6: '21.9% of the manifesting breaking changes are not documented.' arXiv journal-ref: TOSEM 2023, DOI 10.1145/3576037.
correction: Exact quoted wording 'more than one-fifth...' not confirmed; use 'Finding 6: 21.9% of the manifesting breaking changes are not documented.' Authors Venturini, Cogo, Polato, Gerosa, Wiese.

evidence: ISSTA 2017 researchr page (Mostafa, Rodriguez, Wang, UTSA): 68 version pairs of 15 Java libraries; '296 behavioral backward incompatibilities' in 52 of 68 pairs; 'the majority of behavioral backward incompatibilities are not well documented in API documents or release notes'.
correction: Add context: 1,094 test failures/errors; 126 bug reports also studied. Title prefixed 'Experience Paper:'.

evidence: FSE 2024 page (Jayasuriya, Terragni, Dietrich, Blincoe): sample of 30,548 dependencies across 8,086 Maven artifacts; 'We found that 2.30% of these updates had behavioral breaking changes that impacted client tests.'
correction: Also: most such breaks were in non-major updates (violating semver).

evidence: arXiv 2110.07889 abstract: 119,879 upgrades; '83.4% of these upgrades do comply with semantic versioning', contrasting the original Raemaekers et al. study. Serbout&Pautasso Sec 2 and ref [13]: Empirical Software Engineering 27(3), 2022.
correction: Earlier study (Raemaekers) found ~33% of releases breach semver, per Serbout Sec 2. The quoted '293 817 clients' sentence is from Serbout Sec 2, not Ochoa's abstract.
